note: ⚠️ SNG-300 (Erik: 'I want the value and money economy implemented'). PROMOTED FROM po/staged_content — this is the first economy content that is LIVE rather than drafted, and it is what `priceShift` has been waiting for. It supplies three things: the worth bands items now carry, the currencies a purse holds, and the per-region need/scarcity that turns a band into a price.

irreplaceable.note: not for sale — narrative only, and the engine should refuse a price

priceModel.rule: ⚠️ NEED DOMINATES AND `none` IS A HARD ZERO — Erik's correction. If a place does not want a thing, scarcity is irrelevant: nobody bids on what nobody uses. Scarcity only MODULATES an existing need, it never creates one. A one-axis model priced engine parts high in the Quickwood because they are rare there; they are rare there because nobody wants them.
priceModel._bargainDoesNotBank_20260823: ⛔ ERIK'S CLARIFICATION, 2026-08-23. "Not banking the deal" means A BARGAIN NEVER PERMANENTLY CHANGES WHAT A THING IS WORTH — it does NOT mean the engine has no standard pricing. ⚠️ THE ENGINE KNOWS THE STANDARD PRICE AND MUST: `worthBands[item.worth] × need × scarcity` is the honest number the GM quotes, and it is the SAME number the next time anyone asks. A bargain moves what THIS deal settles at and nothing else. ⛔ VERIFIED AT RUNTIME 2026-08-23: standard price 4 before a won bargain, 3.98 settled, 4 again after — `item.worth`, region `need` and `scarcity` all untouched. ⚠️ THE FAILURE THIS FORBIDS: a haggler who talks a merchant down and thereby REPRICES grain for the region. A bargain is a conversation, not an economic event.

currencies.name: Cut crystal
currencies.note: THE REFERENCE CURRENCY. Substrate-inert, standard cut, unforgeable, accepted widest. All rates below are quoted in shards because the world itself would quote them that way.

currencies.name: Old coin
currencies.note: Fixed supply — cannot be minted, only found. Value floats a little on outland demand.

currencies.name: Outland paper
currencies.note: ⚠️ THE ONLY CURRENCY WITH ISSUER RISK. baseValue is a WORLD-STATE VARIABLE, not a constant — a scripted outland event moves it, and that is the one place a 'market' exists in this game.

currencies.name: Reach-scrip
currencies.note: PER-REACH. Tracked as a sub-object keyed by regionId, because a Kept Reach tally and a Stark Reach tally are not the same money.

currencies.name: Marks
currencies.note: ⚠️ NOT DIVISIBLE — a settled obligation is whole or it is nothing. Acceptance is gated on reputation `spread`, not on region: a Mark spends where your deed travelled. Failing the four-of-five test on divisibility is FINE for one currency as a deliberate oddity; it should not be the model for the rest.

the_crossing.note: Takes ALL. The 15% spread IS how the Crossing lives, and it is the only place scrip converts at all.

reaches.spread: n/a — mostly will not convert at all
reaches.note: A party heading into a Reach CONVERTS AT THE CROSSING FIRST or arrives unable to buy bread.

acceptance.workedExample: 20 old coin → crystal at the Crossing: 20 × (6/10) × 0.85 = 10 shards. The 2-shard difference is the Crossing's bite, and it is visible to the player without a percentage ever being quoted at them.
acceptance.erikCallHonoured: The player never sees the number — the trader says 'I'll give you ten for those.' The MATH is concrete; the PRESENTATION stays fictional, which is what Erik asked for earlier.

goodsCategories.name: working nanite devices
goodsCategories.from: precursor salvage — and the outland trade's obsession

holdStore.note: ✅ Q8 (SPEC_hold_store, Erik: 'it should run itself while you're not looking… a thriving mine should make quite a bit of profit'): the store runs on the world tick — yield by condition into holding.store[goods], upkeep from the purse, a full store a target. THE CURVE IS STEEP: thriving is an asset, holding near break-even, strained a subsidy, failing a drain. A unit is worth worthBands[unitWorthBand] × need × scarcity where it is SOLD (regionDemand — the same ore is worth more where it is wanted); you sell where the store stands (holdingOps sell, or the Holdings tab when you are there). Raids: chance = raid.base × dangerLevel × fill, × defendedMult when the hold authors a defence or garrison; a raid takes takeShare and arrives as news. Per tick (72 world hours): thriving 8 × useful 4 = 32 in, 14 out; holding 16 in, 14 out.

keeperMult._note: ⛔ v2 §1 (Erik: 'successful places that don't have a strong leader are targets'): the KEEPER joins the raid product — chance = base × danger × fill × defendedMult × keeperMult[tier]. _none is an UNKEPT hold; _default is a keeper of unknown tier (never read as absent). A full store under Deni Cors is exactly the shape of a target. Priced by CCode; Erik turns.

raid._watches: ⛔ ERIK_holds_features §5 — 'he built the Whistling Woman to watch over it': a hold may carry `watches: <holdId>`. The watched hold's raid chance × watchedMult while the watcher STANDS (not failing, and keeping a watch of its own — stone does not see); × watcherLostMult when the watcher is lost. A reason to defend a post that produces nothing. Priced by CCode; Erik turns.

delegates.note: ⛔ PROPOSAL_delegate_tiers v2 §4 — MY PEOPLE'S PEOPLE (Erik: 'Veth knew him and vouched for him, so that should count too'). A vouch is an ACT in a scene (npcUpdates.vouchedBy), never derived; it needs the voucher's own standing (vouchMinStanding); it is transitive ONCE — a vouched-for person cannot vouch (no chains); the trust it carries is the voucher's standing less vouchDiscount and sits BESIDE the person's own relationship (Aevi §6.1: trusted is not known); it COSTS the voucher vouchFallCost standing when a hold the vouched-for keeps slips on their watch (§6.2 — priced, not ruled). chargeStanding: the trust at which a keeper is a CHARGE-holder (v2 §2, breadth not height) rather than merely keeping — read and said; a charge-holder ACTING on world days is SNG-366's next spec. Priced by CCode; Erik turns.

relay.note: ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-06: 'the relay station income should be enough to maintain the post minimally. The more important the runner post — more messages and traffic — the more revenue; the waygate here will likely bring a lot more runner traffic as word gets out.' A hold with a feature carrying `service: true` (relay_station) earns runner fees each pass: max(feePerPass, its own upkeep) × (1 + trafficPerStation × the other service holds you keep + gateTraffic × ramp), where ramp climbs from 0 to 1 over wordPasses while a NETWORK waygate stands within gateWithinDays of the post. Credited before upkeep as origin 'relay'; said in the news the first time and when word has got out. Priced by CCode; Erik turns.

growth.note: ✅ Q18 (Erik 2026-09-05: 'please build it'; SPEC_hold_store §5): a hold grows by ONE-TIME ACTS WITH LASTING EFFECTS, never a per-tick chore. A KEPT hold climbs one rung every passesPerClimb passes (4 passes = 12 world days) to thriving — and its keeper's TIER sets the FLOOR it will not drop below (floorByKeeperTier; v2 §1: floors, not ceilings). A craft the character carries, applied to the place (the tab, or holdingOps improve), lifts it a rung at once, once per craft per hold, when the craft SHAPES or MENDS (improveFunctions). Each extra hand adds handsYieldBonus to the yield, to maxHands. A garrison halves a raid (raid.defendedMult) and costs garrisonUpkeepPerHand each pass. The ground scales an enterprise's yield by 1 + groundYieldWeight × (density − 0.5): dense lattice 0.9 → ×1.2, thin 0.2 → ×0.85. Priced by CCode; Erik turns them. What a POST can become is not built.

floorByKeeperTier._note: ⛔ PROPOSAL_delegate_tiers v2 §1 (Erik: 'floors not ceilings — poor Deni might just be keeping it, but the place might be thriving anyway due to circumstance'). A keeper sets what the place will NOT DROP BELOW while they are there; circumstance sets the rest. A strong keeper's floor is high — the reward is not permission to climb but that it stays climbed. Read where a hold FALLS (a raid's slip, resolveRaid → advanceHolding); a kept hold climbs to thriving regardless of tier. _default is an unknown tier. Priced by CCode; Erik turns.

debts.note: ✅ Q5-B (SPEC_debts_and_reception, Erik: option B — a PAYABLE debt, and 'tie in the local authority NPC… THEM that will remember what you did… depending on who they are'). worldState.debts[holderId] is held by a NAMED NPC; escalation is THEIR choice: only a holder whose reactsToReputation carries one of escalatingTags acts, one step per escalateAfterDays, up to maxEscalation (1: received colder · 2: refused — no trade, hire or shelter). 3 (a bounty) and 4 (a hit squad) are NOT built — they need an encounter and contingentsFromPeople, and are Aevi's and Erik's to shape. A debt clears three ways: paid (debtOps settle — the purse is debited), a deed (debtOps forgive — the GM says what outweighed it), or the holder dies or departs. Never in coin.

holdFeatures.note: ✅ SPEC_holding_attributes pass two, first cut (Erik 2026-09-05 by example: 'the Threshold Post is supposed to have a mine… a Temple to Attending… Stillwater's Trouble has barriers, a wall, skeletal sentries'). A hold carries FEATURES from this catalogue; each kind names its family (§3 of the spec) and the ONE effect the engine reads for it. material → yields the goods into the store at the hold's condition; martial → the hold is guarded (raids halved) and each defence point cuts a raid's take by defenceShareStep; sentries are a watch that costs no keep; meaning → an aura added to the place's meaningDensity (SPEC_meaning_density — 'a hold IS people living somewhere'); people → quarters raise the hands a hold can work and count as residents; craft → a facility recorded on the place (what it gates is pass three). Priced by CCode; Aevi extends the kinds and their flavour; Erik turns the numbers. A feature is added through play (holdingOps feature) or on the Holdings tab; it records who built it and the crafts used.

workshop.label: a workshop
workshop._yieldFix_20260906: ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-06: 'the workshop says WORKED LIGHT, but a workshop can be for lots of finished goods.' ⚠️ AEVI GAVE IT THE LENS-WORKS' OUTPUT — `worked_light` is what a lens-works makes, and a workshop is the general case. ✅ `mech_parts` is the honest default from the authored goods vocabulary (arms · cut_stone · documents · instruments · living_stock · luxuries · mech_parts · medicines · nanite_tech · precursor_salvage · raw_material · worked_light). ⚑ AND A WORKSHOP SHOULD BE ABLE TO SAY WHAT IT MAKES — see `_yieldOverride`.

quarters.label: quarters — homes for the people who work it

waygate.label: a waygate — made, not found
waygate._note: ⛔ ERIK 2026-09-06: 'A waygate is a huge deal. There aren't many in the world and they let you travel vast distances.' Twenty-seven in the world, and this one was MADE. The effect the engine reads is the PLACE's — journey.gatesUsableBy/routeBetween read `waygate: true` on the location — so the kind marks that the hold KEEPS a gate; nothing new is read. Aevi: the flavour is yours.
waygate._flavour_20260906: ⛑ THE FLAVOUR, AEVI'S, PER CCODE 2026-09-06: 'a `waygate` feature kind now exists — Erik ruled its weight; the flavour is yours.' ⚑ WHAT IT IS TO HOLD ONE: twenty-seven exist in the world and the Precursors made the rest. This one was made by a person, which is either the most reassuring fact in Exesa or the least. ⚠️ A HELD WAYGATE IS NOT A DOOR YOU OWN — IT IS A DOOR THAT OPENS ON YOUR GROUND. The traffic is not yours. People arrive who were not coming to see you, and leave from somewhere you are standing. ⛔ Trade is gated behind wayfaring (`docs/EXESA.md`), so a hold with a gate is not merely richer — it is CONNECTED, and connected places are where things happen to you. ⚑ AND THE KEEPING IS THE POINT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A FEATURE AND NOT A LOCATION FLAG: the gate belongs to the world and reads from the place; the FEATURE says somebody is responsible for it. ⛔ A gate nobody keeps is a hole in the world with weather coming through it. ⚠️ NARRATION: it does not hum, glow, or announce itself. The arch is there and the distance on the other side is wrong, and everyone who uses it stops noticing within a week — which is the strangest thing about it.

keep.label: a keep — the last room that holds

muster_yard.label: a muster yard — where a band forms

hearth.label: a hearth nobody lets go out

kinds._yieldOverride_20260906: ⬜ A FEATURE MAY NAME ITS OWN GOOD. Erik: 'a workshop can be for lots of finished goods.' ⚑ `{kind: 'workshop', yields: 'instruments'}` on the HOLD overrides the kind's default — so Cassiel's workshop at a laboratory post makes instruments, and a wright's workshop makes mech_parts, without two feature kinds. ⚠️ Same shape for `still` (medicines vs luxuries) and `mill` (raw_material vs documents, if it is a paper mill). ⛔ CCode: needs a reader — the kind's `yields` is the default, the feature's own `yields` wins.

watch.label: a Watch — people posted, and they SEE

relay_station.label: a relay station — the network's node

reclamation_bowl.label: a reclamation bowl — where endings are attended

holdFeatures._kindsExtended_20260905: ⚑ AEVI EXTENDED THE KINDS, per CCode: 'Aevi extends the kinds and their flavour; Erik turns the numbers.' +18 kinds, taking the catalogue to 33. ⛔ EVERY ONE NAMES ONE EFFECT THE ENGINE ALREADY READS — nothing here needs a new reader. ⚠️ THREE ADDITIONS CARRY A FLAG THAT DOES: `attends: true` on `temple_to_attending` and `grave_ground`. ⛔ R29 MADE ATTENDING THE MECHANISM AND `the_gathering` STARVES WHERE ENDINGS ARE ATTENDED — so a hold that attends its dead should starve it in its reach. That is the ONE new reader worth asking for, and it is a bestiary term, not an economy one. ⚑ `temple_to_attending` IS ERIK'S OWN EXAMPLE from the Threshold Post. `ward_line` and `sentries` are the Stillwater's Trouble pair — 'barriers, a wall, skeletal undead sentries.' ⚠️ `market` carries `trade: true` and `infirmary`/`longhouse` carry `residents: true`; both are flags for pass three, not readers yet. ⬜ `keep` at defence 3 is the ceiling on purpose — a hold should never be un-raidable, and `minTakeShare: 0.1` already guarantees a raid takes something.
holdFeatures._raid: ✅ R46a (Erik 2026-09-05): A RAID IS A FIGHT, NOT A SUBTRACTION. Undetected, they take what they came for — defenceShareStep still cuts it, and minTakeShare is RETIRED, so stone alone can reduce a take to nothing and a hold with none can lose everything. Detected (a watch: people on the garrison, or a feature that keeps one — sentries, a tower; stone does not see), it is a FIGHT resolved unattended at band scale (melee.legionClash) with the garrison as its actual crew and the raiders drawn from the danger of the place. Win and they take NOTHING and leave spoils behind them — 'not merely the absence of loss'.
holdFeatures._meaning: ✅ R46b (Erik 2026-09-05): A TEMPLE IS NOT DEFINED BY WHAT IT ATTENDS. A meaning feature does three things and `attends` is an optional fourth: it may carry a POWER-SOURCE FIELD (substrateSource {kind: pool|sink, delta} — a hold is a stationary aura, and it may be dense in meaning while thin in apparatus, which is the Numinous's authored problem); it carries an AURA (meaning density, R38); and it DRAWS PILGRIMS, which is a new earning shape — a hold that earns from attendance rather than production, paid in crystal because a pilgrim leaves coin and not ore.

regions.note: ⚠️ THE CROSSING HAS NO DEAD LIST — that IS its identity, expressed mechanically. It is the only place in the world that wants everything, which is why it is the clearing house and why every trade route ends here. It should also never be the BEST price for anything (a 15% spread), so a player who only ever sells at the Crossing is leaving money on the table but never stranded.
Buys raw material and medicines hard (a machine-country grows little and heals badly); sells parts cheap.

⚠️ ERIK'S OWN EXAMPLE, AUTHORED: engine parts are ABSENT here and worth NOTHING — the Quickwood has no use for a directive-core. Scarce and worthless, exactly as he said. A party arriving with a cart of salvage has carried dead weight through a forest.

⚠️ living_stock at HIGH need and ABSENT scarcity = ×5.0, the top of the range: a death-steeped land will pay anything for something that grows. Rootkin seed carried to the Palelands is the single most profitable honest trade in the world, and it is a good one — you are bringing life to a place that has none.
Sells worked light for almost nothing (it is their surplus); buys water-adjacent goods, growth and medicine desperately.

⚠️ A DEAD LIST WITH TEETH: worked light is worth NOTHING in the Umbral Depths — and trying to sell it reads as an insult or a threat. The only dead-list entry in the world that is socially dangerous rather than merely unprofitable.
The crystal-cutters. Buys parts and salvage hard; documents are their surplus and cost nearly nothing here.
Buys RAW MATERIAL at high need — a making-country's appetite is for input. Sells finished goods cheap.

⚠️ THE UNMADE HAS NO USE FOR LUXURIES AT ALL, and that is the sharpest characterisation in the table: a people whose whole craft is careful ending does not buy keepsakes. Everything else is abundant here because they are constantly taking things apart.
Sells arms cheap, buys medicine and food dear — a war-country's economy, and it explains why marchers travel.

⚠️ ARMS ARE WORTH NOTHING IN THE STILLHOLD — a hard zero, and the second socially-loaded dead entry. They will not buy weapons, at any price, from anyone. Directly consistent with the tradition refusing to honour a Marcher oath.

⚠️ A BODY-TRADITION WILL NOT BUY NANITE TECH. The one dead entry that is a PRINCIPLE rather than a lack of use — and it quietly says something about what the Somatics think the Transition did to people.
Buys almost everything at need because they make nothing physical — the purest 'sells services, imports goods' economy in the world.

⚠️ DOCUMENTS ARE WORTHLESS IN THE UNSPOOLING, which is the funniest and most correct entry in the table. A charter means nothing to a chaos-steeped people; you cannot sell a lattice ledger to the Churn. The exact inverse of the Lattice Cities.
Charters are their surplus and cost almost nothing at source — WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY THE LICENCE TRADE IS PROFITABLE ELSEWHERE. The villainy pass and the economy agree.
The Hollow Market. Buys anything, wants luxuries and nanite tech most — appetite as an economy.
No use for luxuries — a truth-people's austerity, and the second region to zero them.
Buys documents at high need — they need real ones to build false ones from. The name-takers' supply chain.
Steady, unhurried demand across the board — patience as an economy.
⚠️ CUT STONE AT `little` NEED AND `absent` SCARCITY — a travelling people does not buy building material. The clearest case of NEED dominating: it is maximally rare here and still nearly worthless.
Stone is their surplus. And note nanite_tech at `little`/`absent` — a concrete-minded people distrusts what it cannot touch.
Second region to zero nanite tech, and for a different reason than the Somatics' — not principle about bodies, but that a meaning-steeped people has no interest in a mechanism.
High need for luxuries and instruments — art and music are not indulgences to a feeling-people, they are infrastructure.

visibility: ⚠️ REQUIRED, per Erik: THE NUMBERS ARE VISIBLE AND PRECISE; THE NARRATION DOES NOT RECITE THEM. Show the purse as a permanent row, show a price as a number when a trade is on the table, and show conversion math so a player can decide whether to convert here or wait. The trader SAYS 'ten for those, and I'm being generous'; the interface SAYS 10. Both.
tradersNotShops: There is no shop screen and there should not be one. A trader is an NPC with wants, and buying is a conversation — which is what this game is good at. The price model exists so the GM has a number to be honest about, not so a UI can render a catalogue.
